answers.answer: Each player takes 12 ordinary turns. Courtship has no player turns, service rotation, monument income, or Servants’ Hall use.
answers.evidence: Overview: ‘each player takes twelve ordinary turns’; ‘Courtship is an event, with no player turns, service rotation, monument income or Servants’ Hall use.’

answers.answer: Hosting order: rotate service (Quarters to Available, then Expended to Quarters); resolve round event; resolve ongoing monument/Servants’ Hall effects; choose activity; invite exactly the required gentry; provide all required service; collect favours (all positive before all negative); optionally buy; then servants go to Expended Service, gentry to personal discard, and tile returns to its tableau column, flipping/upgrading as required. Only the last player advances the marker after cleanup.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure / Player Reference: ‘rotate service → event → ongoing effects → choose tile… positive then negative favours → buy → expend/discard/upgrade.’

answers.answer: Pass order: servants directly to Available Service; gentry in your discard to hand; round-track event then ongoing effects; choose £200 or a free Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; last player advances marker. Butler’s Room hiring is an activity, not a passing benefit.
answers.evidence: Passing: ‘all servants directly to Available Service → all gentry in your discard to hand → round-track event, then ongoing tile effects → choose £200 or a free Market refresh → optional one tile purchase.’

answers.answer: Yes. Screening is fixed after step 2 at 6.1; later Service Help payments can lower actual reputation to 3.4 without invalidating the already-screened PR6 tile or guests. Each Service Help costs 3 increments and moves one servant only from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service; it cannot take a servant from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Reputation screening: ‘fixed at the end of step 2’; remains screening level for whole activity. Service Help: ‘3 increments’ and Quarters to Available only.

answers.answer: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours, choosing order within each group. At minimum reputation you cannot take a negative reputation favour first to avoid a loss; the summary says a negative reputation favour cannot take reputation below 1.1, and positive favours must resolve first. To play a guest with a money penalty, the penalty must be fully payable; use positive money favours, a money VP card, or Borrow Money if short. If still unable to fund it, you cannot play that guest.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 6: ‘Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours.’ Money penalty section: ‘A money penalty must be fully payable.’

answers.answer: Borrow Money: lose 2 reputation increments, gain £100; repeatable. Service Help: lose 3 increments, move one servant from Quarters to Available; repeatable. Refresh Market: lose 4 increments, fully refresh Market; once per turn for this special action. At minimum reputation you cannot take a special action. Service Help cannot take a servant directly from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Special actions table and minimum rule; Service Help entry says ‘cannot take a servant directly from Expended Service.’

answers.answer: Host Butler’s Room with an available butler or underbutler and no gentry. Take up to two servants (not underbutlers) from Servants for Hire into Expended Service, with no fee. On its upgraded side, instead of taking up to two from supply, recruit one common footman, valet, or lady’s maid from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service; unique servants cannot be recruited.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring / Butler’s Room entry.

answers.answer: A housekeeper substitutes for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With Brushing Room in your tableau, a footman substitutes for a valet only when no valets are available. An underbutler can substitute for any base male servant (butler, valet, footman) even if that type is available.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: housekeeper and footman substitution conditions; underbutler may substitute ‘even when that type remains available.’

answers.answer: The only way to acquire an underbutler is to purchase Butler’s Pantry; take one from supply immediately into Expended Service. Normally it moves to Quarters at your next rotation and Available at your second subsequent rotation; passing or Refresh Service VP can make it available earlier, and once in Quarters Service Help or Servants’ Quarters can permit earlier use. Another player cannot recruit it because it is unique, not common.
answers.evidence: Butler’s Pantry entry in Servants and hiring.

answers.answer: Market price is the market-space price plus the tile’s printed modifier. Reserve base price is £300 plus modifier. Price cannot fall below £100. You may not buy a duplicate tile you own; reputation does not restrict purchasing, so a tile above your reputation may be bought.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve: price calculation, £100 floor, no duplicates, reputation does not restrict purchasing.

answers.answer: When a Market space empties, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into the rightmost spaces. A duplicate drawn stacks on its matching Market tile and another tile is drawn; duplicates share one space and its price. Qualifying Reserve tiles go straight to Reserve and another is drawn. If filling multiple spaces, sort only the new tiles by ascending sorting number. Buying one tile from a duplicate stack leaves the space occupied, so there is no refill.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve: Refill paragraph.

answers.answer: After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar to Reserve; later Service draws also go there except Largest Wine Cellar. After courtship 2, also move all Market PR1 tiles there; later PR1 draws go there. Largest Wine Cellar never enters Reserve. A full Market refresh is standard after each of the first three courtships, after Reserve movement.
answers.evidence: Open Reserve and Refresh paragraphs; Overview confirms full seasonal refresh is standard.

answers.answer: At courtship, first return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall. For courtships 1–3, score the current theme category’s tile VP (including negatives; only the face-up hybrid category counts). Highest score gets one VP card and chooses one Fairchild. If tied for highest, each tied player draws a VP card and no one gets a Fairchild. Everyone discards one secret objective; shuffle discards and bottom-deck them. Then open Reserve, fully refresh Market, reveal the next theme to the right of previous themes, pass first-player marker anticlockwise, and advance round marker.
answers.evidence: Courtship and seasonal upkeep: ordinary courtship and upkeep paragraphs.

answers.answer: Final courtship returns Fairchilds as usual and scores tile VP for all four revealed themes; repeated categories count repeatedly, including negative values. Highest gets one VP card and a Fairchild. Tie breaks on highest reputation level, ignoring wheel position; if still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied winners draw VP cards under the courtship tie rule. After discarding the final objective, players get a final chance to use special actions and VP cards for benefits where possible; then move marker to Wedding Bells and score.
answers.evidence: Final courtship (round 16) paragraph.

answers.answer: VP categories: improvement tiles (face-up printed VP, including negatives and unused); gentry in hand and discard (including family and final Fairchild, excluding dismissed guests); fulfilled objectives; reputation level; servants; wealth; retained VP cards. Reputation levels 1–7 score 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28 VP; wealth is 1 VP per £200 rounded down. Victory ties: final Fairchild, then highest reputation level, then shared victory. Wheel position does not affect reputation VP or break ties.
answers.evidence: Final VP table and tie paragraph.

answers.answer: Normally five objectives at setup plus two at round 6, discarding one at each of four courtships, leaving three to score. Extra objectives from Main Library or a VP card add to retained final objectives and do not cause an extra discard. Shuffle simultaneous discards together, then put them face down on the bottom of the objective deck. Tile objectives require owning tiles at game end, not upgraded tiles.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards paragraph.

answers.answer: A VP card benefit may be used immediately when drawn, at any time on your later turn (several cards allowed), and once more after final courtship before scoring. Used cards go to the bottom of the VP deck; retained unused cards stay hidden with objectives and score their printed VP. You cannot take both benefit and final VP.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards: VP card rules.

answers.answer: Normal activity tiles must flip to the rose/upgrade side after first use; an already-upgraded normal tile stays upgraded on later uses. Hybrids start with underlined icon up and flip after every use, moving to the newly face-up category. A tile upgrading into a monument (Queen’s Suite or Lionheart Suite) hosts its front activity once, upgrades to ongoing monument, and can never host again. For hybrids, only the currently face-up category counts at courtship and for objectives.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects: normal, hybrid, and monument rules.

answers.answer: Monuments and Servants’ Hall resolve in the ongoing-effects step on hosting and passing turns, after the round-track event; no ongoing income/use occurs during courtship. Servants’ Hall uses one available servant placed on it to lower one opponent’s reputation by one and gain one yourself; that servant cannot serve the activity and goes to Expended Service at turn end. You cannot target a player at minimum reputation.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects: monuments and Servants’ Hall entries; turn structure sets timing.

answers.answer: Heritage Guest Suite: one footman on tile, one casual guest from hand with normal guest service; doubles all guest favours including negative ones; upgrades and remains an activity tile. Queen’s Suite: housekeeper, one prestige guest from hand with normal service; doubles one chosen favour and resolves others normally; upgrades into monument. Lionheart Suite: butler, draws one prestige guest to attend with no personal guest service; doubles nonnegative favours, excludes negative favours from doubling; retain guest and put it in discard at cleanup; upgrades into monument. All have a fixed one-guest count that cannot be changed.
answers.evidence: Suite activity table and following fixed-count paragraph.

answers.answer: A random player gets first-player marker. Starting to that player’s left and going clockwise, each chooses an available base family board. Bonuses: Asquith adds Dowager Countess; Cavendish starts at reputation 1.4; Ponsonby gets £300; York gets a footman in Available Service.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 5.

answers.answer: Each player starts reputation level 1, position 1; use 1/2, 3/4, 5/6 and Max counters with 1 showing and Max at bottom; do not use 7/8 counters. They receive one butler, housekeeper, valet, lady’s maid and footman in Available Service; Private Study, Butler’s Room, Main Gazebo, Front Parlour and Bowling Green with starter/building icon showing; and Lord, Lady, Heir and Young Lady family cards. Only Ponsonby starts with money, £300 (York instead gets a footman; others no money). Asquith’s fifth family card is Dowager Countess.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2, 3, and 5.

answers.answer: For three players: three valets, three lady’s maids, six footmen, and two underbutlers in Servants for Hire; no butlers or housekeepers. Unused servants are returned to the box and unavailable this game.
answers.evidence: Setup step 6 gives one valet and lady’s maid per player, two footmen per player, two underbutlers total; no butlers/housekeepers; unused servants unavailable.

answers.answer: Separate starter guests from casual deck, shuffle them, and deal two to each player; shuffle every unused starter back into the casual deck. Starter guests are casual guests with a starter icon and otherwise follow normal casual rules, not a separate guest type during play.
answers.evidence: Setup step 4; Gentry section says starter guests are casual guests with starter icon.

answers.answer: For four players, select one double-sided monument per player plus one: five total. Choose at most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze. Tiles that later upgrade into monuments always go in the bag and do not count against the setup selection.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7 states ‘one double-sided monument per player plus one,’ at most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze, and later-upgrading tiles always go in bag and do not count. It does not explicitly say whether they stay out of the bag; it says they always go in.

answers.answer: Fill six different eligible spaces with tiles PR3 or less (including no PR), excluding Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments. Set aside ineligible draws and return them to the bag after filling; stack duplicates in the same space. Normal tiles enter with upgrade/rose icon hidden; hybrids with underlined hybrid icon showing. Sort spaces by ascending sorting number from the £300 space. PR4 tiles, Servants’ Hall, and double-sided monuments are ineligible.
answers.evidence: Setup step 8.

answers.answer: Set Alderley Hall standard side up, round marker at 1, and one reminder token per player above the track. Shuffle theme and VP decks separately; reveal first theme for open courtship, keep revealed themes in order through the game; place base Charles and Elizabeth Fairchild face up on Alderley Hall. First theme is not hidden, and old revealed themes remain in order rather than leaving play.
answers.evidence: Setup step 9.

answers.answer: During rotation, the servant in Quarters moves to Available Service, and the servant in Expended Service moves to Quarters. Each advances exactly one space; do not move expended servants twice. An unused available servant remains available.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 1: rotation order and ‘Unused available servants remain available.’

answers.answer: No immediate Fair reward if Private Study is not upgraded at the event check. You may upgrade/use it later that turn, but that does not retroactively grant the reward. An already-upgraded Study gives £300 and 2 reputation on Village Fair spaces 3 and 9 only.
answers.evidence: Round-track events table: Village Fair spaces 3 and 9; reward only if Study already upgraded at that step. Private Study entry confirms reward.

answers.answer: Round 6 Draw Objectives event resolves before ongoing tile effects, during hosting after service rotation or during passing after servants and gentry return. Draw two objectives and keep both secret with your objectives. It applies on each player’s turn, including passing players.
answers.evidence: Round-track events order and table: round 6 draw two and keep both; events happen on each player’s turn; passing resolves event.

answers.answer: Yes. National Holiday waives PR on all tiles and guests when hosting, so low-reputation players may play higher-PR ones. All other requirements remain binding, including service and exact gentry count/types.
answers.evidence: Round-track events table and National Holiday text.

answers.answer: Yes, during Builders’ Holiday you may buy any number from Market and/or Reserve within funds, but finish all purchases before sliding/refilling. Prices remain the Market-space/Reserve base plus modifier that applied before the sequence; no price shift or refresh between purchases. The Reserve can be included. Market Purchase VP-card benefit follows the same single-unchanged-market rule, including no refresh between purchases.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase VP card paragraph.

answers.answer: Set all Market tiles aside, leave Reserve unchanged, refill all six spaces from the bag under normal refill rules and sort new tiles, then return set-aside tiles to the bag and mix. Set-aside tiles cannot reappear during that same refresh. Reserve tiles remain unchanged.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve: Refresh paragraph.

answers.answer: Each reputation symbol is one increment; clockwise gains and anticlockwise losses. Crossing position 5 to 1 raises a level; crossing 1 to 5 lowers one. A full level is five increments. Minimum is 1.1; maximum is 7.5 (Max.5) in standard play; ignore losses beyond minimum. At Max.5 excess is lost unless spent immediately on special actions; you may take actions before or during a reputation favour to create space.
answers.evidence: Reputation, wealth and special actions section.

answers.answer: Money is public. Players may not give or receive money between themselves. Never spend more than you have. The money supply is unlimited; use proxies if needed.
answers.evidence: Money held is public paragraph.

answers.answer: Ladies includes every female family member or female guest, so family can fill a ladies requirement. Casual-guest requirements require casual guests and exclude family. Exact printed number/types are mandatory; no extra or fewer gentry. Family needs no personal service and has no PR; the activity tile and played guests otherwise must pass reputation screening (unless National Holiday waives PR).
answers.evidence: Hosting step 4 and reputation screening section.

answers.answer: For screening, draw the stated number, choose the stated number to keep, reveal only kept cards, and add them to hand; rejected cards go to the bottom of their guest deck unrevealed. For an ordinary guest invite, the summary says newly invited guests are drawn from the indicated deck, revealed to everyone, and added to hand. The requested detailed ordinary-invite procedure beyond that is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 6 gives ordinary new guest invite reveal/add-to-hand; Gentry section gives screening draw/keep/reveal and rejected-card destination.

answers.answer: Dismissal is optional, so with no unwanted guests you need not dismiss. You may dismiss an eligible guest from hand, current activity, or discard, including one drawn earlier in Enjoy Favours. Family cannot be dismissed. The dismissed guest goes to the bottom of its matching deck, is no longer yours, does not return on passing, and does not score for you later.
answers.evidence: Gentry section: dismissal rules.

answers.answer: Lord: £200. Lady: choose screen two casual guests/keep one, or optionally dismiss one guest. Heir: choose £100 or one reputation. Asquith Dowager: both £100 and one reputation. Lady and Heir offer choices; Lord gives one benefit; Dowager gives both.
answers.evidence: Base family card table.

answers.answer: She gains the admirer bonus only when a male prestige guest attends the same activity. Bonus is two reputation. With male casual guest, female prestige guest, or Charles Fairchild (a male prestige guest), she still draws one casual guest; Charles qualifies as male prestige.
answers.evidence: Family card table: Young Lady draws one casual guest and gains two reputation if a male prestige guest attends; Gentry section identifies Charles as male and prestige.

answers.answer: Charles gives three reputation; he is a male prestige guest with no PR and requires a valet. Elizabeth gives both one prestige guest and two reputation; she is a female prestige guest with no PR and requires a lady’s maid. They are prestige guests, not family cards; the summary says family can never be dismissed but does not explicitly state Fairchild dismissal immunity, so that part is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Gentry section says Fairchilds are prestige guests with no PR; Charles valet, Elizabeth lady’s maid; family cannot be dismissed. Fairchild dismissal immunity is not explicitly addressed.

answers.answer: Miss Elizabeth Perkins reduces one opponent by one reputation. Miss Florence Oliver reduces one opponent by two reputation and you lose one yourself. Minimum-reputation protection applies, so a player at 1.1 cannot be targeted by an opponent’s reputation-reducing effect.
answers.evidence: Gentry section: base gossip cards; Reputation section: at minimum cannot be targeted by opponent reputation-reducing effect.

answers.answer: Barn earns one reputation each time you host an Estate activity. It gives nothing merely for owning an Estate tile or when passing.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects: Barn entry.

answers.answer: Each turn the Servants’ Quarters tile lets you use one servant from Quarters in addition to Available Service, without reputation payment. This occurs after ordinary rotation and is distinct from Service Help, which costs 3 increments to move one Quarters servant to Available. The servant used through the tile goes to Expended Service at turn end.
answers.evidence: Servants’ Quarters tile entry.

answers.answer: Front-side Private Study requires two family and a butler, has no tile favour, and upgrades permanently into an ongoing tile. You cannot repeatedly host it once upgraded; its ongoing side gives £300 and two reputation only on Village Fair rounds, without hosting it again.
answers.evidence: Private Study entry.

answers.answer: Unupgraded Main Library: butler and two family; draw one extra objective. Upgraded: butler and three family; draw one VP card. The extra objective increases the number retained for final scoring; it does not cause an extra discard.
answers.evidence: Main Library entry; Objectives section says extra objectives add to final retained count without extra discard.

answers.answer: Objective VP benefit: draw two objectives, keep one, return the other to the bottom of the objective deck. This gives one additional retained objective for final scoring.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table: Objective.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Service moves all servants directly to Available Service, including those in Expended Service, usable immediately. Service Help instead costs 3 reputation increments per servant and moves one only from Quarters to Available, never directly from Expended.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table: Refresh Service.

answers.answer: Hire Servant takes one servant from Servants for Hire, not an underbutler, into Expended Service. It cannot provide service immediately from there; ordinary rotation moves it to Quarters first, then Available at the subsequent rotation (unless an effect/pass makes it available earlier). The ordinary availability timing follows service rotation rules.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table says source and destination and excludes underbutler; hosting rotation says one space per rotation. Immediate usability is not stated in the Hire Servant entry, but Expended Service is not Available Service.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Guest returns one gentry, including a family member, from personal discard to hand. If returned before Invite Gentry, you may choose it to attend this activity subject to normal requirements; returning it does not automatically play it.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table: Refresh Guest.

answers.answer: The basic-servant objective counts only common footmen, valets, and lady’s maids; it excludes butler, housekeeper, and underbutler. Ordinary service VP awards 2 VP for every servant in employ, all types and locations. The ten-servant objective awards 7 VP for at least ten servants total.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference and Final VP table.

answers.answer: Monument objective counts 3 VP per monument, including upgraded Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite. Category objectives count tiles currently in the specified category; only the face-up category counts for a hybrid.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: monuments; Improvements and ongoing effects: hybrids count their current face-up category.

answers.answer: Nature Group is 11 VP for Flower Room plus one of English Garden, French Garden, Sculpture Garden, or Garden Maze. Domestic Group is 12 VP for Gabled Conservatory plus Main Library or North Library. They need not have been used; owning the tiles at game end suffices.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference group list and owning tiles rule.

answers.answer: Prestige-guest objective gives 1 VP per prestige guest; the every-three-guests objective gives 1 VP per complete group of three nonfamily guests. Final Fairchild counts as a prestige guest. Incomplete groups score nothing.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: guest bonuses; Fairchilds are prestige guests; objective says per complete three guests.

answers.answer: The reputation objective earns 7 VP for reaching maximum reputation level 7, regardless of wheel position. The wealth objective earns 10 VP for at least £1200. Wheel position does not change ordinary reputation VP or break reputation tie resolution; only level is used.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference; Final VP reputation table and tie paragraph.

answers.answer: Both West Terrace sides require one butler and exactly three family cards. Unupgraded favour: draw one prestige guest. Upgraded favours: draw one prestige guest and optionally dismiss one to four guests from hand, current activity, or discard to the bottom of their appropriate decks. It remains an activity on both sides and never becomes an ongoing dismissal tile.
answers.evidence: West Terrace paragraph under Improvements and ongoing effects.

answers.answer: There is no maximum hand or personal discard-pile size. Gentry in discard still belong to you and score normally.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family: ‘There is no hand or discard-pile limit’ and discard-pile gentry score normally.

answers.answer: You may inspect all Reserve tiles and buy any one, including a tile underneath another in a stack; there is no top-tile-only restriction. Every Reserve tile is public and available for selection.
answers.evidence: Open Reserve paragraph.

answers.answer: You are not required to host when able; hosting says if required gentry or service are unavailable, choose another legal activity or pass, and if no activity is possible you must pass. Thus you can choose to pass; if a preferred activity lacks attendees or servants, choose another legal activity or pass.
answers.evidence: Hosting steps 4–5: if unable, choose another legal activity or pass; passing procedure is available.

answers.answer: Yes. On a pass you may take the free Market-refresh benefit, use the paid special-action refresh, and use multiple Market Refresh VP cards in the same turn, subject to purchase-timing restrictions. The once-per-turn limit applies only to the special-action Market Refresh; free pass refreshes and VP-card refreshes do not use it.
answers.evidence: Special actions section: other refresh methods do not use once-per-turn special refresh allowance; multiple Market Refresh VP cards allowed; pass refresh can combine with paid special refresh.
